newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ fires minister in bid to steady coalition govt.
newsitem.headline: NZ fires minister in bid to steady coalition govt.

text.p: New Zealand's Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters on Thursday fired a junior cabinet minister in a bid to calm tensions straining the country's fledgling coalition government.
Peters said he fired Associate Health Minister Neil Kirton, a member of Peters' own New Zealand First party, "in the interest of good government".
The move followed a drawn-out dispute over duties between Kirton and senior Health Minister Bill English, who is from the larger party in the centre-right coalition, the National Party.
Peters told a news conference he was sacking Kirton for breaking an agreement not to speak to the media until after top-level talks among cabinet ministers had finished.

"Last night I made it very clear to Mr Kirton that there was to be no media comment pending a meeting between the Prime Minister and myself to sort out the public dispute between the two health ministers," Peters said in a statement.
"This morning Mr Kirton went on radio in disregard to that clear instruction and accordingly I have dismissed him."
Prime Minister Jim Bolger, who leads the National Party, and English declined to comment on the affair, and Kirton was due to hold a news conference later in the day.
Parliamentary sources told Reuters that Kirton was expected to announce he was considering resigning from parliament -- which he would have to put before the speaker.
The troubles over Kirton are rooted in the handling of a number of health policy issues where Kirton has publicly crossed swords with English.

In the latest exchanges, English had commented on national radio that rules needed to be laid out for ministerial conduct because of what he called "public questions about the ethical principles of New Zealand First".
Peters said he had made the decision to remove Kirton without prior reference to Bolger and in the interests of the country, the government, New Zealand First and the health portfolio.
Kirton is a so-called "list" MP for NZ First following last October's general election. List MPs are used to top up a party's representation to reflect its share of the overall vote.

The election was the first under a system of proportional representation, and left NZ First in a crucial position to affect the balance of power. The coalition government was eventually formed in December.
In the 120-seat single chamber parliament National has 44 and NZ First 17 seats, giving them a narrow voting majority.
According to the rules, if Kirton were to resign his seat he would be replaced by the next person on the NZ First party list, leaving the overall balance of power unchanged.
